title: SpaceX Faces Wall Street for the First Time as Stock Slides Below IPO Price
excerpt: The world's most valuable aerospace company reports its inaugural quarterly earnings today, with shares down roughly 15% from their June IPO and a massive lock-up expiration looming.
body:
• SpaceX reports its first-ever quarterly earnings on August 4, 2026, roughly two months after its June 12 IPO at $135 per share.
  • Shares have fallen approximately 15% from the IPO price, trading around $114-118, amid broader concerns about the "Elon premium" wearing thin.
  • Analysts expect revenue of approximately $6.8 billion for Q2, with AI-related revenue from the xAI merger nearly tripling to an estimated $2.33 billion.
  • A lock-up expiration beginning August 6 could allow insiders to sell shares, adding further pressure to the stock.

SpaceX goes before public market investors for the first time today, and the reception may not be warm. The company, which went public on June 12 at $135 per share, reports its inaugural quarterly earnings with its stock trading well below the IPO price and a lock-up expiration just two days away.

The report will offer the first detailed public accounting of SpaceX's finances since Elon Musk's sprawling aerospace and AI conglomerate — formed through the February 2026 merger of SpaceX and his AI venture xAI — entered the public markets with a valuation exceeding $1.5 trillion.

What Analysts Expect

Wall Street consensus projects revenue of approximately $6.72 to $6.8 billion for the second quarter, with an expected loss per share of $0.26, according to estimates compiled by Zacks Investment Research and other tracking services.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=KSznXlUxcjQ

The most closely watched line item will be AI revenue, inherited from the xAI side of the business. Analysts expect AI-related revenue to reach roughly $2.33 billion, nearly tripling from the prior quarter. Starlink, the satellite internet division that represents SpaceX's most mature consumer business, is expected to show continued subscriber growth, having reached 10.3 million users with an EBITDA of $2.1 billion in Q1 2026.

"The Elon Premium isn't what it once was."

— Bloomberg analysis, August 2026

The Stock Under Pressure

SpaceX's IPO was one of the most anticipated public listings of the decade. The company priced at $135, valuing the combined entity at more than $1.6 trillion. But the stock has struggled since, falling into the $114-118 range, a decline of roughly 13-15% that has frustrated early investors and raised questions about whether the company's sprawling ambitions justify its valuation.

Part of the pressure comes from the impending end of the post-IPO lock-up period. Starting August 6, insiders and early investors will be free to sell their shares for the first time. Lock-up expirations routinely create selling pressure even for well-performing stocks, and SpaceX's below-IPO trading adds an additional layer of uncertainty.

Capital spending has also drawn scrutiny. In Q1 2026, SpaceX reported AI-related capital expenditures of $7.72 billion, a figure that dwarfs its AI revenue and reflects the enormous cost of building out the compute infrastructure inherited from xAI. Investors will be looking for signs that this spending is translating into customer commitments and revenue growth, not just capacity expansion.

Starlink Remains the Bright Spot

While the AI business carries the growth narrative, Starlink continues to be the financial engine. The satellite internet service has grown subscribers by an estimated 52.6% year over year and has achieved consistent profitability at the EBITDA level. Starlink's expansion into aviation, maritime, and direct-to-cell services has broadened its addressable market well beyond rural broadband.

For the Indian diaspora, Starlink's global expansion plans carry particular weight. The service has been seeking regulatory approval in India for years, and its eventual entry could reshape internet access in underserved regions where the diaspora maintains strong ties.

A Test of the Musk Premium

The earnings report arrives at a complicated moment for Musk's public market standing. Tesla's stock has also faced headwinds, and the concentration of Musk's attention across SpaceX, xAI, Tesla, and his government efficiency advisory role has raised governance questions among institutional investors.

For SpaceX, the stakes are straightforward: the company needs to convince Wall Street that the combination of rockets, satellites, and artificial intelligence represents a coherent business with a credible path to profitability, not just the world's most expensive science fair project. Today's numbers will be the first real test.
